title: Body cues, not facial expressions, discriminate between intense positive and negative emotions.
central_claims: At intense emotional peaks, body context discriminates positive from negative affect more reliably than isolated faces.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. SSRP supplementary methods and Tables 1, 3 and 4
source_manifest.finding: Body-context valence discrimination reproduced independently: r=.829, p<.001, N=14; this tests intense expressions, not the claim that faces never convey emotion.

source_manifest.title: Out of Context, Beyond the Face: Neuroanatomical Pathways of Emotional Face-Body Language Integration in Adolescent Offenders
source_manifest.finding: Independent investigators explicitly used tasks based on Aviezer et al. stimuli to measure contextual emotion processing in 35 adolescent offenders and 30 controls.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating the replicability of social science experiments in Nature and Science between 2010 and 2015
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent replication reports positive significant focal results for both Aviezer and Karpicke/Blunt in Figure 1. Original-author reviewed protocols; not every original experiment was repeated.

source_manifest.title: Pillaud, Chassaing-Monjou and Cottin: I React to Bodies but not Faces, Replication and Extension of Aviezer et al., 2012
source_manifest.finding: Conference author abstract page 178 reports a preregistered independent replication of Experiment 1 (N=194) plus four affective-task extensions. Bodies rather than isolated faces discriminate peak-emotion valence. Conference report; not full methods.

source_manifest.title: Pillaud et al. I react to bodies but not faces, a replication and extension of Aviezer et al. (2012), Emotion, doi:10.1037/emo0001621
source_manifest.finding: Read the complete author abstract as indexed by OpenAlex: five experiments replicate Experiment 1 and extend to affective priming, misattribution, feelings and action tendencies; body-only stimuli consistently produce the effects. Same research program as P, not a third group.
